title: EXP-042 — Hello World Part 1: Two Test Records Through the Web Client Runtime
objective: In the authenticated DEM configuration, use only the existing User-scope Form FX_HelloWorld01, bound to IDO FX_HelloWorld01 and table dbo.FX_HelloWorld01, to enter exactly two factory-owned test records: FX_Code=FX001 with FX_Label=Factory test one, and FX_Code=FX002 with FX_Label=Factory test two. First verify that the collection contains zero existing persisted rows and establish the identity of both unlabeled runtime inputs through supported visible or accessibility evidence corroborated by the Designer component bindings and FX_Code Required property. Enter the first record, use the native New action to stage the second record, and perform exactly one explicit toolbar Save. Verify the committed values, ordinarily close the runtime Form, reopen it once, and query all records to verify both values are recovered. Record the inserted rows in the cleanup inventory. Classification is observed only, not replay_verified.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, the Hello World Part 1 tutorial test-data section at 7:40–8:01, EXP-040, EXP-041-R3, and their decisive evidence before browser actions.

Standard input methods (record each use): the Select Form filter needs key-event typing (browser_type with slowly: true, EXP-041); Mongoose combobox and wizard fields take one plain fill (browser_type without slowly, EXP-041-R3). For each runtime edit field use one plain fill into the verified input, then press Tab once to commit; take a fresh snapshot and confirm the field shows the exact value before moving on. If a value does not stay in its field after one corrected attempt, stop before Save. Before every prompt or alert click, take a fresh snapshot and confirm the button label of the exact ref.
Use the existing authenticated DEM configuration G6R8LJ9Q4E8C2Z8Y_MONGOOSE_DEM_DEFAULT and existing Site Developer/User-scope context. Do not perform authentication or session replacement.
Confirm that the prior EXP-041-R3 runtime tab and its untouched blank record have been closed by the operator. If still open, stop without discarding it or opening a duplicate runtime Form.
Read-only verification of the existing FX_HelloWorld01 Form identity, User-scope version, Primary Collection FX_HelloWorld01, generated component bindings and clean Designer state.

Read-only reference to the established FX_HelloWorld01 IDO and dbo.FX_HelloWorld01 table definitions from EXP-040. FX_Code is String 30, required and the primary key; FX_Label is String 100 and nullable.

Open FX_HelloWorld01 exactly once in the Web Client using Select Form. If filtering is needed, use Filter By Name, Case Sensitive unchecked, Starts With unchecked, and the verified Control+a plus key-event typing method. Verify the intended Form before confirming the selection.

Before data entry, use a supported read-only collection query, such as Filter-in-Place F4 with empty criteria, to establish that zero persisted records exist. Capture the settled grid and any record count or empty-result indication. A starred blank new row alone does not prove an empty collection. If the query does not establish emptiness, stop.

Before typing, identify which actual runtime input binds to FX_Code and which binds to FX_Label using supported rendered or accessibility information and the established Designer component properties. Corroborate FX_Code using its Required property. Record the exact observable mapping. Do not rely solely on input position, asterisk location or assumptions inherited from EXP-041-R3.

Verify the runtime is ready for new-record entry. If the empty-collection query changes the mode, use only a supported visible New control to enter add mode, recording the action and state. Stop if that transition cannot be verified.
Enter record 1 with FX_Code FX001 and FX_Label Factory test one. Capture both values and the associated input identities before advancing.

Use the native toolbar New once to begin record 2, provided record 1 remains safely staged and New has not unexpectedly committed or discarded it. Enter FX_Code FX002 and FX_Label Factory test two. Capture the two staged records before Save.

Perform exactly one explicit runtime toolbar Save after both records are staged, using a freshly verified Save control. Record the exact response, alerts, validation messages and post-Save state. Do not retry after timeout or uncertain completion.
Verify the saved collection displays exactly two records with the expected FX_Code and FX_Label pairings, with no duplicate or unexpected rows.

Close the clean runtime Form through its ordinary Form-tab close control exactly once, reopen FX_HelloWorld01 once through the supported Select Form route, and query all rows with an empty Filter-in-Place criterion or supported refresh. Compare the returned rows with the post-Save baseline.
Capture screenshots and accessibility snapshots showing target identity, field mapping, initial zero-row condition, both staged records, the Save result, post-Save rows and post-reopen rows.
Record the two FX_ test records in evidence/EXP-042/cleanup-inventory.md. Confine repository changes to the EXP-042 experiment record and evidence/EXP-042/.

Before every prompt or alert response, obtain a fresh snapshot and verify the exact accessible button label and reference. Allow at most one fresh recovery snapshot and one corrected visible inspection; stop if the postcondition remains unproven.

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight evidence establishes a usable authenticated DEM configuration, expected User-scope FX_HelloWorld01 Form and matching Primary Collection/IDO, clean Designer state, and no leftover runtime draft requiring worker disposal. The authorized target table and two record values are documented before any application data mutation.

A supported read-only query of the target runtime collection visibly establishes zero existing persisted records before entry. Evidence identifies the Form and query result, distinguishes the new-row placeholder from persisted rows, and records zero matches for existing FX001 and FX002. Any existing record or unprovable empty state closes the mutation gate.

Pre-entry screenshots or accessibility snapshots establish an unambiguous FX_Code-to-input and FX_Label-to-input mapping, corroborated by the existing Designer bindings and FX_Code Required property. The worker records the exact identifying evidence rather than inferring a mapping from control position. If the runtime controls cannot be identified, this check fails and no typing occurs.
The first staged new record visibly contains FX_Code FX001 and FX_Label Factory test one in the verified corresponding inputs. No other record or field is modified, and no explicit Save has occurred.

The supported New action advances to the second staged record without unexpectedly discarding or committing record 1. Evidence captures record 2 with FX_Code FX002 and FX_Label Factory test two, while confirming both expected records remain represented before Save. Any unexpected persistence or loss is recorded as a blocker.

Exactly one explicit runtime Save is performed after both records are staged. The captured response and settled runtime state show successful completion without validation or duplicate-key error. No retry, second Save or application-data edit occurs.

Immediately after Save, a supported complete collection read displays exactly two persisted records, pairing FX001 with Factory test one and FX002 with Factory test two. Both values, count and target Form identity are directly captured; absence of additional rows is established for the queried collection.

Exactly one ordinary runtime Form-tab close and one supported reopen recover FX_HelloWorld01. An unfiltered complete collection query after reopen returns exactly the same two records and values as the post-Save baseline, with no extra rows or errors. Evidence establishes same-session runtime recovery only.

The evidence/EXP-042 cleanup inventory contains exactly the two inserted rows, their table and IDO identities, exact values and cleanup ownership, with no deletion performed. The final experiment record contains an AC-1 to AC-9 matrix, screenshots and snapshot references, operation counts, Save outcome, repository-confinement audit, error/recovery accounting and final browser state. Findings are classified observed only.

initial_instruction: T1 — READ-ONLY PREFLIGHT; NO DATA ENTRY OR SAVE. Read AGENTS.md, the tutorial test-data section, EXP-040 and EXP-041-R3, including their decisive evidence and documented limitations. Create the EXP-042 record and evidence directory. Verify the inherited browser/session state, confirm the operator has closed the prior blank runtime draft, and establish the exact User-scope FX_HelloWorld01 Form and existing FX_HelloWorld01 IDO/collection identity. Open the target Form through the supported Web Client Select Form route at most once, using the verified key-event filter method. Establish collection emptiness through a supported complete read-only query; a starred blank row is insufficient. Then inspect the two runtime input controls read-only and attempt to prove their individual FX_Code and FX_Label identities through supported rendered/accessibility information corroborated by the existing Designer bindings and FX_Code Required property. Capture target identity, zero-row evidence, exact control mapping and current mode. Do not type, use New to stage a record, Save, or otherwise mutate application data in T1. If the empty-collection or field-identification gate cannot be proven, stop and document the blocker; do not guess or attempt alternate unsupported methods. Record decisive screenshots, accessibility evidence, operation counts, limitations and the current browser state under EXP-042 only. Later insertion, the single Save, and close/reopen verification require separate bounded worker instructions after these gates pass.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261010-154641-QsiV. Rationale: EXP-040 established the FX_HelloWorld01 SQL table and IDO, and EXP-041-R3 successfully created the User-scope FX_HelloWorld01 Form, verified its FX_Code and FX_Label bindings, recovered it across ordinary Designer close/reopen, and opened it in the Web Client. The next tutorial step is to enter test data. This experiment tests exactly one bounded two-record insertion workflow using the existing Form and IDO. The principal safety gates are proving the collection initially contains zero persisted records and identifying the two unlabeled runtime inputs before any typing. Previous runtime evidence did not independently expose their field names, so that identification cannot be assumed. If either gate fails, stop without writing data. | Operator review: exact-value and no-JavaScript guards added; standard input methods added (filter: key events; fields: one plain fill plus Tab, verified). Approved by the operator 2026-10-10.
